title: Espaces stratifiés et voisinages côniques (ou : déploiement des espaces stratifiés) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context. In the surrounding notes Grothendieck builds, for a stratified space with 'locally cylindrical' structure (strata of codimension 1 meeting transversally, as in a manifold with corners or a normal-crossings configuration), the spaces Γ(d) = Σ^∨(d+1). These are spaces of ordered d-tuples of distinct germs of codimension-1 strata at a point, with Γ'(d) ≅ S_d × Γ(d) (formula (35) on p.54). He also describes a 'relative total order' on Γ_0 = Σ^∨(1) over Σ. That order is a clopen half Γ_1 of Γ_0 ×_Σ Γ_0 minus the diagonal, satisfying the transitivity condition (36).

On this page he says he has 'batifolé', mixing three things: purely set-theoretic properties of the ordered set Σ, semi-simplicial interpretations, and topological aspects. He then restarts axiomatically.

Setup. Σ = Σ(0) is an ordered set with a topology (not necessarily Hausdorff). Σ(1) ⊂ Σ×Σ is the graph of the order relation.

Axiom (a), topological. The target ('but') projection b: Σ(1) → Σ(0), (y≤x) ↦ x, is proper and locally an immersion, i.e. locally injective, with finite fibres.
- Consequence 1: the diagonal Σ → Σ(1) is a section of b, so it is open in Σ(1).
- Consequence 2: if Σ is Hausdorff the diagonal is also closed, hence clopen. One may then set Σ*(1) = Σ(1) minus the diagonal, the graph of the strict order.
- Consequence 3: properness of b plus Hausdorffness give that Σ(1) is closed in Σ×Σ.

Axiom (b), set-theoretic. For every x the lower set Σ_{≤x} is totally ordered (and finite). So the order is a 'forest' order whose down-sets are finite chains.

Axiom (c), begun at the bottom of the page and continued on p.56. Simplices x_{i0} < … < x_{id} of the nerve ending at x correspond to subsets of cardinality d+1 of the chain Σ_{≤x}, of cardinality N(x).

Consequence (p.56).
- Σ*(d) is the space of strict chains x0 < … < xd, with target map Σ*(d) → Σ, (x0,…,xd) ↦ xd.
- The fibre over x is a set of d-subsets of a finite chain.
- The whole semi-simplicial space (Σ*(d))_d, with its face maps, is reconstructed from the single relative object Σ*(1) → Σ*(0) together with its relative total order.

Geometric meaning (p.56, axiom (C)). The points of Σ*(1) over x index the local branches B_α at x (codimension-1 strata germs). These branches are required to be mutually transversal, and the points of Σ*(d) over x index intersections of branches. Thus the axioms package the situation of the boundary of a manifold with corners, or the normalization tower of a normal-crossings divisor: ∂X → X is a proper immersion, and ∂^k X → X parametrizes k-tuples of distinct local boundary components. Choosing a relative total order makes this tower semi-simplicial rather than merely S_d-equivariant.

Purpose. To obtain a clean, minimal axiomatics for the combinatorial-topological skeleton of the 'déploiement' (unfolding / conical neighbourhoods) of stratified spaces.
errors: Minor indexing issue (visible on the next page): if N(x) = card(Σ_{≤x}) counts x itself, the fibre of Σ*(d) → Σ over x is the set of d-subsets of Σ_{<x}, which has N(x)−1 elements, not N(x). The p.56 formula P_d({1,…,N(x)}) is off by one unless N(x) means card(Σ_{<x}).

The openness of the diagonal needs only local injectivity of b: a continuous section s of a locally injective map p has open image, since s(W) = U ∩ p^{-1}(W). Grothendieck's inference is correct. Closedness of the diagonal and of Σ(1) in Σ×Σ needs Hausdorffness, which he correctly adds as a hypothesis ('Si Σ est séparé').
Item ⓑ is duplicated: the first ⓑ was abandoned ('par l'explicit…' struck) and the label reused. Item ⓒ is unfinished on this page.

ideas.what: Axiomatize the boundary structure of a 'locally cylindrical' stratified space by a proper, locally injective, finite map b: Σ(1) → Σ(0) (the graph of an order with finite chain down-sets). Here the diagonal is clopen and the complement Σ*(1) parametrizes local branches.
ideas.modern_name: Boundary ∂X → X of a manifold with corners as a proper immersion; local boundary components; normalization of a normal-crossings divisor
ideas.usually_credited_to: Douady (1961, variétés à bord anguleux), Cerf; systematized by Joyce (2009-2012, 'On manifolds with corners'); Deligne (Hodge II) for normal-crossings divisors
ideas.where_published: Not in his published texts to my knowledge. Esquisse d'un programme §5-6 discusses 'tame' stratified spaces and déploiement only programmatically.

ideas.what: The tower Σ*(d) of strict chains (d+1-fold intersections of branches) as a semi-simplicial space, reconstructed from the single relative object Σ*(1) over Σ plus a relative total order. Without the order one only has Γ'(d) ≅ S_d × Γ(d).
ideas.modern_name: Semi-simplicial resolution of a normal-crossings / corner configuration; nerve of a locally finite forest order; ∂^k X and C_k(X) = ∂^k X / S_k in Joyce
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne (Hodge II/III, ordered components); Joyce for ∂^k X with free S_k action

ideas.what: Separation of the axioms into purely order-theoretic (down-sets are finite chains), semi-simplicial, and topological (properness and local immersion of the target map) layers.
ideas.modern_name: Posets with tree-like down-sets / forest orders; exit-path style combinatorics of stratifications

missed.claim: Grothendieck independently arrives, c.1981, at the now-standard structure of the boundary of a manifold with corners: a proper immersion ∂X → X whose k-fold iterates parametrize ordered k-tuples of distinct local boundary components, with a free S_k action (Γ'(d) ≅ S_d × Γ(d)). He adds an axiomatic, purely topological characterization: a proper locally injective target map with clopen diagonal, plus totally ordered finite down-sets. Joyce's later formalism is close; the 'relative total order ⇒ semi-simplicial space' packaging is a mild variant not usually stated this way.
missed.quote: Σ_{(1)} →(b.pr.) Σ_{(0)} est propre et loc. immersif ... Pour tout x∈Σ, l'ens Σ_{≤x} est tot. ordonné pour l'ordre induit.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical: it shows the corners/boundary-immersion formalism (Joyce, Kottke–Melrose) present in Grothendieck's unpublished work on tame topology/déploiement. Mathematically it is mostly known material, so its value is chiefly priority and context.

deep.surprise_reason: A clean re-axiomatization of the branch/corner structure underlying his déploiement programme. The mathematics (proper immersion of local boundary components, ordered intersections as a semi-simplicial space) is close to Douady/Deligne/Joyce material and largely routine, though its appearance here, predating Joyce, is a minor historical point.
transcription_corrections: 'Σ = Σ(ω)' should be read as 'Σ = Σ(0)' (the zero-level space, consistent with the 'Σ_(0)' written under the equals sign below).
Line 4: 'propriétés purement ensemblistes de l'ens. ordonné' is correct. The struck word after Σ is likely 'leur'.
'Σ ens. ordonné, muni d'une topologie [-séparée-] (pas ...)' should read '...(pas nécessairement séparée)' (the replacement is probable).
Over the arrow 'b. pr.' most likely means b = 'but' (target projection, as on p.56), with 'pr.' = projection. 'loc. immersif borden[?]' likely ends with 'borné' or a finiteness qualifier.
'dans si Σ séparé, une diagonale' should read 'donc, si Σ séparé, la diagonale [est] une partie à la fois ouverte et fermée'.

'Si Σ est séparé, la propriété de Σ(1) → Σ(0) implique aussi que Σ_1 est fermé dans Σ×Σ': the insertion above 'Σ×Σ' replaces the struck 'Σ(0)×Σ(0)'. The '(fini)' and '(fibré ...)' marginalia are uncertain.
Item ⓒ reads approximately: 'Dans le domaine d'un diagramme x_{i0} – x_{id} de longueur d dans Σ_≤, équivalent : celles d'une partie de card. d+1 [de l'un des N(x) éléments]'.
